chunks: Then al-‘Alā’ said to him: O’ Amīr al-mu’minīn, I want to complain to you about my brother ‘Āṣim ibn Ziyād.
ai.seo_question: Who did al-‘Alā’ complain about to the Imam in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This opening incident in the *Sermon of the Vast House* establishes the historical context of the Umayyad governor’s opulence as a catalyst for Imam Ali’s (AS) critique of worldly attachment. It highlights the Imam’s role not only as a political leader but as a spiritual guide addressing the moral decay of the elite, setting the stage for his famous metaphor of the world as a 'house' with a 'door' to death.
